items.title: 'Genius' novel sold in major six- and seven-figure deals at auction pulled over AI allegations
items.excerpt: A crime novel that secured major six- and seven-figure deals in the US and UK has been withdrawn from sale after allegations that AI was used in its creation, with the agent pulling the book from circulation. A sharp real-world case of AI provenance and disclosure disrupting acquisition and editorial workflows in trade publishing.

items.title: Tor Bramble backs H M Wolfe after AI-detection claims over Daggermouth
items.excerpt: Publisher Tor Bramble publicly backed author H M Wolfe after her dystopian romance Daggermouth scored 60% on the AI-detection tool Pangram (as first reported by The Atlantic), spotlighting how unreliable AI detectors are becoming a live craft-and-trust problem for authors and editors. A concrete look at AI-detection tooling colliding with the writing and publishing process.

items.title: Researchers attempt to prove that generative AI dilutes the market for books
items.excerpt: A new study tries to put empirical numbers on a fear authors have voiced for years: that the flood of generative-AI-written books measurably shrinks the market and attention available to human-authored work. A creative-industry counterpart to the AI-detection studies the beat already runs, framing how AI-generated output reshapes what gets read and sold.

items.title: Poetry Foundation Library Scraped, Used to Make AI-Generated Educational Content
items.excerpt: Giggle Academy, a 'free learning' platform founded by Binance's CZ Zhao, scraped hundreds of copyrighted poems from the Poetry Foundation to auto-generate illustrated lessons and storybooks with no human curation. A concrete look at AI-generated creative/educational content at scale, and what fully-automated book-making does to poets and publishers.
